excerpt: Storm-damaged panel fencing along a rear garden in Hersham replaced with closeboard on concrete posts, finished in three days.

faqs.answer: With concrete posts and gravel boards the timber stays off the ground, so fifteen years or more is typical with basic care.
faqs.question: How long does a closeboard fence last?

faqs.answer: No. The posts & gravel boards are concrete and every bay is <2m tall, which is within the usual limit for a rear garden.
faqs.question: Did this fence need planning permission?

faqs.answer: Yes. Here it was stepped down the slope in equal bays so the top line looks even from the house.

sections.answer: A storm had brought down most of the old panel fencing along the back garden. The customer wanted a boundary that would stand up to wind and keep the dog in.
sections.question: What did the customer in Hersham need?

sections.answer: The garden slopes away from the house and the old timber posts had rotted below ground, so nothing could be reused. Access was through a narrow side passage.
sections.question: What made this fence difficult?

sections.answer: We stepped the fence down the slope in even bays and used concrete posts with concrete gravel boards, so no timber sits in the wet ground.
sections.question: How did we solve it?

sections.answer: We removed and recycled the old panels and posts, dug and concreted fourteen new posts, fitted gravel boards and built closeboard bays on site with capping rails.
sections.question: What work was carried out?

sections.answer: The garden has a straight, solid boundary that follows the slope neatly. The work took three days and the dog is safely back in the garden.
sections.question: How did it turn out?

social.caption: A storm took down this back garden fence in Hersham. We replaced it with closeboard on concrete posts, stepped neatly down the slope. Three days from start to finish.
